name: Robotics & Automation
tagline: Build machines that sense, think and act — from factory arms to delivery robots and humanoids.

overview.summary: Robotics engineers design, program and test robots: industrial arms in factories, autonomous mobile robots in warehouses, drones, agricultural robots, surgical systems and, increasingly, humanoids. The field combines mechanical design, electronics, control theory and software — especially perception (computer vision), motion planning and, more and more, AI models that let robots learn skills. Industrial automation (PLCs, robotic cells) is the most common job path; AI-driven 'physical AI' is the most hyped.
whyTrending: 'Physical AI' became a major investment theme in 2025–26: foundation models for robots (e.g. NVIDIA Isaac GR00T, Google's Gemini Robotics) and well-funded humanoid start-ups are hiring robotics software engineers.
Labour shortages and reshoring push manufacturers and warehouses to automate, keeping demand high for automation and controls engineers.
BLS projects mechanical engineers — the occupation that includes many robotics engineers — to grow 11% from 2025 to 2035, much faster than average.

In Bangladesh, the garment (RMG) and manufacturing sectors are adopting automation to stay competitive, and university robotics teams have built a strong talent pipeline through international competitions.

roles.title: Robotics Software Engineer
roles.description: Writes the software for robot perception, planning and control, usually with ROS 2, C++ and Python.

roles.title: Automation / Controls Engineer
roles.description: Programs PLCs, industrial robots and production lines in factories and warehouses.

roles.title: Perception / Computer Vision Engineer
roles.description: Builds the vision and sensor-fusion systems (cameras, LiDAR, IMU) that let robots understand their surroundings.

roles.title: Motion Planning & Controls Engineer
roles.description: Designs algorithms that make robots move safely and precisely — trajectories, kinematics, feedback control.

roles.title: Robot Learning Engineer
roles.description: Trains robots with reinforcement learning, imitation learning and simulation-to-real transfer.

roles.title: Robotics Test / Field Engineer
roles.description: Integrates, tests and maintains robots at customer sites, diagnosing hardware and software issues.

beginner: Electronics basics: circuits, sensors, motors, microcontrollers (Arduino)
Linear algebra, trigonometry and basic physics
intermediate: ROS 2: nodes, topics, services, launch files
Simulation with Gazebo or NVIDIA Isaac Sim
PLC programming basics (ladder logic) for industrial roles
advanced: State estimation and sensor fusion (Kalman filters)
Reinforcement and imitation learning for manipulation
Vision-language-action models and robot foundation models

stack.note: C++ + Python + ROS 2 is the core of robotics software listings. Industrial automation roles instead emphasise PLC platforms (Siemens, Rockwell) and industrial robot brands (ABB, FANUC, KUKA).

roadmap.title: Electronics and programming
goals: Build simple Arduino/ESP32 projects: LEDs, sensors, motors
Strengthen Python and learn C++ basics
Review linear algebra and trigonometry for coordinate frames
Learn Linux basics (ROS runs on Ubuntu)
Build a line-following or obstacle-avoiding robot car
roadmap.milestone: A working small robot car with sensor-based behaviour and a demo video.

roadmap.title: ROS 2 and simulation
goals: Complete the official ROS 2 beginner tutorials
Simulate a mobile robot in Gazebo
Implement PID control for speed or heading
Use OpenCV to detect objects or follow a coloured target
Run Nav2 navigation with a simulated map
roadmap.milestone: A simulated robot that maps a room and navigates to goals autonomously.

roadmap.title: Manipulation and AI
goals: Simulate a robot arm with MoveIt and plan pick-and-place
Try a reinforcement learning task in Isaac Lab or Gymnasium
Move one project from simulation to real hardware
Join a robotics competition team or open-source ROS project
roadmap.milestone: A pick-and-place demo (sim or real) and a portfolio page with videos and code.

projects.title: Obstacle-avoiding robot car
projects.description: Arduino or ESP32 car with ultrasonic sensors that avoids obstacles and can be controlled by phone over Bluetooth.

projects.title: PID balancing or line-following robot
projects.description: Tune a PID controller for smooth line following or self-balancing and plot the error over time.

projects.title: ROS 2 autonomous navigation
projects.description: Build a simulated (then real, if possible) mobile robot that runs SLAM, builds a map and navigates with Nav2.

projects.title: Vision-based sorting arm
projects.description: A robot arm (sim or low-cost real arm) that detects coloured objects with OpenCV and sorts them with MoveIt.

projects.title: Learned manipulation policy
projects.description: Train a pick-and-place policy with imitation or reinforcement learning in simulation (Isaac Lab / LeRobot) and evaluate sim-to-real transfer.

interview.question: What is ROS 2 and why use it?
interview.answer: A set of libraries and tools for robot software with a publish–subscribe communication system (nodes, topics, services, actions). It provides drivers, visualisation, simulation integration and reusable packages.

interview.question: Explain a PID controller.
interview.answer: It computes a control signal from the error between target and actual value: Proportional reacts to current error, Integral removes steady-state error, Derivative dampens fast changes.

interview.question: Forward vs inverse kinematics?
interview.answer: Forward kinematics computes the end-effector pose from joint angles; inverse kinematics finds joint angles that achieve a desired pose — often with multiple or no solutions.

interview.question: What is SLAM?
interview.answer: Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping: building a map of an unknown environment while estimating the robot's position in it, using sensors like LiDAR or cameras.

interview.question: What is a Kalman filter used for?
interview.answer: Estimating a system's state (e.g. position, velocity) by combining a motion model with noisy sensor measurements, weighting each by its uncertainty.

interview.question: What is the sim-to-real gap?
interview.answer: Differences between simulation and reality (physics, sensor noise, lighting) that make policies trained in sim fail on real robots. Domain randomisation and real-world fine-tuning help.

interview.question: How do you make a robot safe around people?
interview.answer: Risk assessment, speed and force limits, safety-rated sensors and stops, collaborative-robot modes, redundancy and following standards like ISO 10218 / ISO/TS 15066.

interview.question: What is a PLC?
interview.answer: A Programmable Logic Controller: a rugged industrial computer that reads sensors and controls machines in real time, programmed in ladder logic or structured text.

interview.question: How would you debug a robot that drifts off its path?
interview.answer: Check sensor calibration and odometry, compare commanded vs actual wheel speeds, inspect localisation estimates, tune the controller and test components in isolation.

interview.question: What are degrees of freedom?
interview.answer: The number of independent ways a robot can move. A typical industrial arm has 6 DOF, enough to reach any position and orientation within its workspace.

bangladesh.note: Paylab Microcontroller Programmer range (10th–90th percentile, gross monthly) — the closest published category. Automation engineers at large factories and multinational suppliers may earn more; robotics R&D roles are still scarce locally.

remote.note: Estimate. Most robotics jobs are on-site because they involve hardware; remote opportunities exist in simulation, perception, ROS software and robot-learning roles.

sources.label: Arc — Remote software engineer salaries in Bangladesh

global.benchmark: US median, Mechanical Engineers incl. robotic engineers (BLS, 2025)
global.note: Robotics software engineers at tech and autonomy companies often earn closer to software-developer pay ($134,040 BLS median for the combined category).

demandNotes.bangladesh: Growing slowly. Factory automation (RMG, pharma, food processing), electronics manufacturers and a few robotics start-ups hire; competition-team experience helps.
demandNotes.remote: Limited because of hardware needs, but simulation, perception and ROS software contracts exist.
demandNotes.global: Growing strongly in automation, warehouses and AI-driven robotics; humanoid and physical-AI start-ups are well funded but concentrated in the US, China, Europe and Japan.
